1. This revision petition is directed against the order of Ld. trial court passed on 08.10.2015 in the case titled "State Vs. Anjali Roy Chaudhary & Ors.", FIR No. 26/2000, P.S. Lodhi Colony, whereby Ld. trial Court found sufficient material on the record to frame charge against the petitioner under section 420/120-B IPC and against order dated 10/08/2016 vide which the charge was framed.

sentences.text: 2. Shorn of unnecessary details, alleged facts of the case qua the petitioner are that she was director of M/s Intcargo Clearing Agency (P) Ltd., which maintained a current account No. 666 with the complainant bank.
Arti Mitra Vs. State Page no.1 of 11

On 07.05.1993, the M/s Intcargo Clearing Agency (P) Ltd.,
presented certain cheques for encashment vide two deposit vouchers/pay-in-slip for the sum of Rs.
75,640 and Rs. 2,26,407.
The cheques were sent in clearing for encashment and as per the rules and procedure, the amount was credited in the account of M/s Intcargo Clearing Agency (P) Ltd. on 08.05.1993.
However, the cheques, which were presented for encashment, vide the above said two pay-in-slips, received back dishonoured including two cheques of Rs. 75,640 and of Rs. 1,76,407.

As per the rules, the account of M/s Intcargo Clearing Agency (P) Ltd. should have been debited with the amount of the dishonoured cheques, but instead of debiting the current account of M/s Intcargo Clearing Agency (P) Ltd. for Rs. 2,52,047.00 (Rs. 1,76,407.00 + Rs.75,640.00), the Imprest Clearing Account of complainant bank was debited with such amount.

However, on the same day, a sum of Rs. 50,000 towards the other two cheques of Rs. 25,000 each,
was debited in the said account of M/s Intcargo Clearing Agency (P) Ltd. because those cheques had also been received back dishonoured.

On inquiry, it was revealed that though initially a debit voucher for an amount Rs. 2,52,047 was filled in for debiting account of M/s Intcargo Clearing Agency (P) Ltd., by using the words "C/A 666 Int Cargo Clg A" yet later the name of M/s Intcargo Clearing Agency (P) Ltd. was struck down in furtherance of the criminal conspiracy and the amount was illegally debited in the Imprest Clearing Account, maintained by the complainant bank, by interpolating the words "Imp. Clg" in the debit voucher.
The said voucher was approved and passed by Arti Mitra Vs. State Page no.2 of 11 the then Branch Manager Sh. Prem Singh Chauhan (Accused No. 04 in the charge sheet).

sentences.text: It was also revealed that on 08.05.1993, M/s Intcargo Clearing Agency (P) Ltd. was having a clear balance of Rs. 1,05,238.42 in its account.
Out of which, M/s Intcargo Clearing Agency (P) Ltd. got issued a draft of Rs. 1,00,000/- and hence a sum of Rs. 1,00,025/- was debited in the aforesaid account.

Though on the said date there was not sufficient clear balance in the aforesaid account of M/s Intcargo Clearing Agency (P) Ltd. yet Sh. Prem Singh Chauhan (Accused No. 04 in the charge sheet), the then Branch Manager, ignoring all the banking norms and rules, cleared the cheque for Rs. 2,81,674/- resulting into wrongful gain to M/s Intcargo Clearing Agency (P) Ltd. and wrongful loss to the complainant bank.

On inquiry, it was known that the account opening form as well as specimen signature card relating to M/s Intcargo Clearing Agency (P) Ltd. were missing from the records of the bank and it was done to destroy the evidence against the culprits.

It was also revealed that a Current Account No. 406 in the name of Intcargo Clearing Agency, a proprietorship concern of Sh. Swapan Mitra, the husband of Ms. Arti Mitra/Petitioner, having the same address as of M/s Intcargo Clearing Agency (P) Ltd.
was opened on 09.04.1989 and was closed on 07.09.1989.

Again, on l1.02.1990 a Current Account No. 436 was opened in the name of Intcargo Clearing Agency, a partnership concern of Smt. Arti Mitra/petitioner and Ms. Anjali Roy Chaudhry (Accused No. 01 in the charge sheet), operating from the same address.

The complainant bank did not have the account opening form of the Arti Mitra Vs. State Page no.3 of 11 said account CA No. 436, as well, which was closed on 11.11.1992 after transferring Rs 52.430.75 to Current Account No. 666 which is in the name of M/s Intcargo Clearing Agency (P)Ltd.

Counsel for petitioner argued that admittedly, the cheques in question were presented on 07.05.1993 and returned after dishonour to complainant bank on 01.05.1993, hence, it is impossible that the irregularities were noticed by the bank officials for the first time on 17.02.1998 i.e., about five years after the return of the cheques.

He argued that between May 1993 and February 1998, at least four annual audits of the complainant bank's record must have taken place and it is not possible that such irregularities were not noticed in Arti Mitra vs State on 19 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177565369/

sentences.text: these audits and therefore the allegations, as levelled belatedly on 11.12.1999, are an afterthought.
He also argued that no intimation regarding the dishonour of the cheques was ever given to the account holder.
Moreover, the bank had not initiated any proceedings against the concerned account holder for recovery of the amounts of the dishonoured cheques.

He further argued that an account holder is not aware of any account called the "Imprest Account",
which is internally Arti Mitra Vs. State Page no.4 of 11 maintained and managed by the bank and such account is not accessed by the account holder.

entities.text: Arti Mitra Vs. State Page no.4 of 11
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Moreover, an account holder is also not a privy to the books maintained by the bank and therefore he cannot be liable for any errors or discrepancies in such books.

It was also argued that there is no material on record to either to show that who was responsible for the affairs of M/s Intcargo Clearing Agency (P) Ltd. or to show anything suggesting a criminal conspiracy between the petitioner and the other accused.
5.

Per contra, Ld. Addl. P.P for the state/respondent argued that there is sufficient material on record to frame charge against the petitioner and the impugned order is correct and does not suffer from any illegality.
6. I have heard the arguments and have gone through the Ld. trial court record.

7. In the State of Maharashtra & Ors. Vs. Som Nath Thapa & Ors. AIR 1996 SC 1744, it was observed by Hon'ble Apex Court that if the court were to think that the accused might have committed the offence it can frame the charge, though for conviction the conclusion is required to be that the accused has committed the offence.

entities.text: State of Maharashtra & Ors. Vs. Som Nath Thapa & Ors. AIR 1996 SC 1744
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is apparent that at the stage of framing of charge, probative value of the materials on record cannot be gone into and the materials brought on record by the prosecution has to be accepted as true at that stage.

8. Further, in the State of Rajasthan Vs. Fatehkaran Arti Mitra Vs. State Page no.5 of 11 Mehdu,
(2017) 3 SCC 198, Hon'ble Apex Court has held that scope of interference under Section 397 Cr.P.C,
at a stage, when charge had been framed, is well settled and at this stage, the court is concerned not with the proof of the allegation rather it has to focus on the material and form an opinion whether there is strong suspicion that the accused has committed an offence, which if put to trial, could prove his guilt.

entities.text:
State of Rajasthan Vs. Fatehkaran Arti Mitra Vs. State Page no.5 of 11 Mehdu,
(2017) 3 SCC 198
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The framing of charge is not a stage, at which stage the final test of guilt is to be applied.

Thus, to hold that at the stage of framing the charge, the court should form an opinion that the accused is certainly guilty of committing an offence, is to hold something which is neither permissible nor is in consonance with the scheme of Code of Criminal Procedure.

9. Moreover, in Amit Kapoor vs. Ramesh Chander and Another, (2012) 9 SCC 460, Hon'ble Apex Court also held that the object of section 397 CrPC is to set right a patent defect or an error of jurisdiction or law.

entities.text: Amit Kapoor vs. Ramesh Chander and Another, (2012) 9 SCC 460
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There has to be a well founded error and it may not be appropriate for the court to scrutinise the orders, which upon the face of it bears a token of careful consideration and appear to be in accordance with law.

The revisional jurisdiction of the higher court is very limited one and Arti Mitra vs State on 19 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177565369/
3 where the Court is dealing with the question as to whether the charge has been framed properly and in accordance with law in a given case, it may be reluctant to interfere in exercise of its revisional jurisdiction.

entities.text: Arti Mitra vs State on 19 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: No meticulous examination of the evidence is needed for considering whether the case would end in conviction or not at the stage of framing of charge or quashing of charge.

Another very significant caution that the courts have to Arti Mitra Vs. State Page no.6 of 11 observe is that it cannot examine the facts, evidence and materials on record to determine whether there is sufficient material on the basis of which the case would end in a conviction; the Court is concerned primarily with the allegations taken as a whole whether they will constitute an offence and, if so, is it an abuse of the process of court leading to injustice.

entities.text: Arti Mitra Vs. State Page no.6 of 11
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Where the offences is even broadly satisfied, the Court should be more inclined to permit continuation of prosecution rather than its quashing at that initial stage.
The Court is not expected to marshal the records with a view to decide admissibility and reliability of the documents or records but is an opinion formed prima facie.

10. In Asim Shariff vs. National Investigating Agency, (2019) 7 SCC 148, it was held by Hon'ble Apex Court that it is expected from the trial Judge to exercise its judicial mind to determine as to whether a case for trial has been made out or not.

entities.text: Asim Shariff vs. National Investigating Agency, (2019) 7 SCC 148
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: But at the same time, it also held that it is true that in such proceedings, the Court is not supposed to hold a mini trial by marshalling the evidence on record.

11. In Mahendra Prasad Tiwari vs. Amit Kumar Tiwari and Ors, Crl. Appeal No. 1210/2022 decided by Hon'ble Apex Court on 12.08.2022, it was held that the truthfulness, the sufficiency and acceptability of the material produced at the time of framing of a charge can be done only at the stage of trial and at the stage of charge the Court is to examine the materials only with a view to be satisfied that prima facie case of commission of offence alleged has been made out against the accused person.

entities.text: Mahendra Prasad Tiwari vs. Amit Kumar Tiwari and Ors, Crl. Appeal No. 1210/2022
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Arti Mitra Vs. State Page no.7 of 11 12.

Hence, considering the law laid down in the aforesaid judgements, it is clear that at the stage of framing of charge, the court has to see only a prima facie case against the accused and it is not supposed to examine the facts, evidence and materials on record to determine whether there is sufficient material on the basis of which the case would end in a conviction.
13.
It means that if the evidence available on the record prima facie shows that there is likelihood that it can be proved during trial, the charge should be framed.

14. In the instant case, on the one hand, it has been argued by the Ld. counsel for the petitioner that there is no material on record to show as to who was responsible for the affairs of M/s Intcargo Clearing Agency (P) Ltd. but on the other hand, in clause (B) of the grounds for revision, it is mentioned that that no intimation regarding the dishonour of the cheques was ever given to the concerned account holder.

In view of above said arguments and the submissions made in the petition, the question arises, if the petitioner was not the director of M/s Intcargo Clearing Agency (P) Ltd., then how does she know that no intimation regarding the dishonour of the cheque was given by the complainant bank to the Arti Mitra vs State on 19 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177565369/
4 account holder?
It prima facie shows that the petitioner was the director of M/s Intcargo Clearing Agency (P) Ltd. and therefore she is aware of the factum of such non-issuance.

Even otherwise at the stage of the framing of charge the court is required to consider only the police report and the documents sent with it and if these materials lead to grave Arti Mitra Vs. State Page no.8 of 11 suspicion against the accused, charge must be framed.
15.

operating from the same address.
